issues.summary: The step-up does not check that the prior session belongs to the same user or was an OIDC session: any valid gateway cookie (another user's, or a SIWE session) passes, and its exp is carried over.
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.service.ts:231-243 only calls decodeToken(...).exp, and no auth_method/sub comparison with userId (resolved at :149) is done anywhere. So the docblock's promise at :183-191 that it 'elevates the session the user already has' is not enforced. The integration test (spec:737-741) even signs a random sub, and the unit tests never check sub, so a regression here would go unnoticed. The impact is limited because MFA is still required and the old behaviour minted a fresh session anyway.

issues.summary: assertExpirationTime still runs on Auth0's exp on the elevate path, even though that value is discarded in favour of the prior expiry; there is no test for this interaction.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.service.ts:134-140 runs before getSessionExpiration (:142), and on elevation the expirationTime is ignored (:208-220). This check predates the PR and applied to elevation before too. It only bites when Auth0's ID-token exp exceeds the configured max validity, which is unlikely.

issues.summary: The absolute-timeout rationale is repeated across several docblocks.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.service.ts:91-94, :183-186 and :226-228 do restate the same reasoning, but this is only documentation redundancy with no functional cost.

issues.summary: The clamp uses a Date comparison instead of Math.min.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.service.ts:216-220 is correct and readable; this is pure style.

issues.summary: The integration spec hand-builds the prior-session payload instead of using oidcAuthPayloadDtoBuilder.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.controller.integration.spec.ts:737-741 uses faker for sub and a minimal payload for jwtService.sign. It is not a literal fixture, so this is a consistency preference only.

issues.summary: Claim that the PR title is a capitalised, non-imperative noun phrase.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The actual PR title is 'fix(auth): keep the prior session expiry on step-up', which is lowercase, imperative and conventional-commit style.

issues.summary: The decode-failure debug log has no contextual prefix.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.service.ts:241 logs only asError(err).message at debug level. Adding context would be nicer, but a debug line has little concrete cost.

issues.summary: The unit test throws a generic Error rather than TokenExpiredError.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The catch at oidc-auth.service.ts:238-242 has no error-type-specific logic; it handles any error the same way. So a generic Error exercises exactly the real path.

issues.summary: Over-max exp raises ForbiddenException while a missing session raises UnauthorizedException.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The ForbiddenException comes from the pre-existing shared assertExpirationTime (token-expiration.utils.ts:14), which is also used by SIWE login. Both errors are redirected to the client the same way, so the difference is stylistic.

issues.summary: The 'no session to elevate' negative path is tested at both the unit and integration layers.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: oidc-auth.controller.integration.spec.ts:813 and service.spec.ts:621 overlap, but the integration test also covers the controller passing the cookie (or its absence) through, so the redundancy is cheap and arguably useful.

issues.summary: getSessionExpiration throws but is not named with an OrFail/assert prefix.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: No such naming convention is documented in docs/agents, and the @throws is clearly documented at oidc-auth.service.ts:188-191.
